questions.q: What is the contextual meaning of 'क्सèkwfy csyk' as used in the opening paragraph of 'नवलजीत नसोनक्ल'?
questions.a: Correct answer: 'क्सèkwfy csyk' refers to the leisurely, rhythmic passage of time or movement, specifically the elephant's slow, swaying walk that marks time passing. A wrong answer like 'slow walk' misses the nuance of 'ले;' (time/rhythm) and the cultural association of an elephant's gait with majestic, unhurried time. This reveals the student is translating word-for-word instead of reading the scene.

questions.q: In the sentence 'गज़ब cgl' (गज़ब गज़ब), why does the author repeat 'गज़ब' instead of using a synonym like 'आश्चर्य' or 'विस्मय'?
questions.a: Correct answer: The repetition mimics the oral storytelling style and emphasizes the mahout's stunned disbelief through rhythm, whereas a synonym would feel like a narrator's commentary. A wrong answer focusing only on 'emphasis' misses the performative, folk-narrative function. This shows the student treats vocabulary as interchangeable labels rather than stylistic choices.

questions.q: The word 'चकित' appears when Lakhho reacts to the child's appearance. Using the glossary definition ('आँखें फैल जाना' / sudden wide-eyed surprise), write a new sentence where a different character experiences 'चकित' due to a sound, not a sight.
questions.a: Correct answer: 'अचानक बिजली कड़की और यमुना चकित होकर द्वार की ओर देखने लगी।' (Sudden lightning struck and Yamuna, wide-eyed with surprise, turned toward the door.) A wrong answer would use 'चकित' as a synonym for 'confused' or 'scared' without the physical marker of sudden arrested attention. This reveals the student misses the visuo-sensory specificity of the word.

questions.q: Analyze the cultural specificity of 'उह्यकटफी' (uhykatfy). Why does the author choose this regional term over the common 'रजाई' or 'कंबल' in the monsoon night scene?
questions.a: Correct answer: 'उह्यकटफी' denotes a light, starched cotton quilt used specifically in humid monsoons — unlike winter 'रजाई' (heavy, for cold) or 'कंबल' (woolen, generic). The author chooses it to signal: (1) season (rains), (2) Ikbal's professional knowledge as a mahout who knows elephants need breathable cover in humidity, (3) the daily ritual of care (starching, airing). A wrong answer treating it as 'just a blanket' erases the cultural precision that characterizes the human-animal bond. This shows the student reads vocabulary as decorative rather than world-building.

questions.q: Evaluate whether the glossary definition of 'वलीक्वव' (vLiqQV) as 'स्पष्ट, मगर थोड़ा-थोड़ा अटककर' adequately captures its effect when Lakhho speaks to the police officer in the climax.
questions.a: Correct answer: The definition is necessary but insufficient. 'वलीक्वव' in that scene carries moral weight: Lakhho's 'clear-yet-hesitant' speech signals truthfulness without performance. It contrasts with the officer's expected bureaucratic fluency. A student who only paraphrases the glossary ('he spoke clearly but with pauses') misses how the word redistributes authority — the villager's imperfect speech becomes more credible than official language. This reveals the student cannot yet connect micro-vocabulary to macro-theme.

questions.q: Create a 3-sentence mini-scene using 'थककर बैठ जाना' (th [kksydj nsuk) to show a character's emotional surrender, not just physical tiredness. The character must not be elderly.
questions.a: Expected answer criteria: (1) Character faces a recurring, systemic struggle (e.g., a young farmer facing loan rejection, a student failing a third attempt). (2) 'थककर बैठ जाना' is the climax of the scene, not the opening. (3) The surrender is conscious — 'बैठ जाना' is a chosen stop, not a collapse. Poor answer: 'रमेश दौड़कर थककर बैठ गया।' (Merely physical). Good answer: 'तीसरी बार बैंक से खाली हाथ लौटकर, रमेश ने अपनी फाइल बरामदे की खाट पर रख दी और वहीं थककर बैठ गया — इस बार खेत बेचने का इरादा लिए।' This shows the student can transfer the word's psychological valence to a new context.
